metadata.title: On the Brunn-Minkowski inequality for general measures with applications to new isoperimetric-type inequalities

nodes.name: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for a measure in a class $\mathcal{K}$
nodes.statement: A Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfies the Brunn-Minkowski inequality in class $\mathcal{K}$ if for all $A,B \in \mathcal{K}$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$: $\mu(\lambda A + (1-\lambda)B)^{1/n} \geq \lambda \mu(A)^{1/n} + (1-\lambda)\mu(B)^{1/n}$.

nodes.name: Unconditional function
nodes.statement: A function $f:\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ is unconditional if $f(\varepsilon_1 x_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n x_n) = f(x)$ for all sign choices $\varepsilon_i \in \{-1,1\}$.

nodes.name: Decreasing unconditional function
nodes.statement: An unconditional function $f$ is decreasing if for each $i$, $t \mapsto f(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1},t,x_{i+1},\ldots,x_n)$ is non-increasing on $[0,\infty)$.

nodes.name: Ideal (class $\mathcal{K}_I$)
nodes.statement: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is an ideal if $\mathbf{1}_A$ is unconditional and decreasing; equivalently, $(x_1,\ldots,x_n) \in A$ implies $(\delta_1 x_1,\ldots,\delta_n x_n) \in A$ for all $\delta_i \in [-1,1]$. The class is denoted $\mathcal{K}_I$.

nodes.name: Symmetric convex set (class $\mathcal{K}_S$)
nodes.statement: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is symmetric if $A = -A$. The class of symmetric convex sets is denoted $\mathcal{K}_S$.

nodes.name: Unconditional measure
nodes.statement: A measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is unconditional if it has an unconditional density.

nodes.name: Geometric mean of sets
nodes.statement: A family $\odot = (\odot_\lambda)_{\lambda \in [0,1]}$ of maps $\mathcal{K} \times \mathcal{K} \to \mathcal{K}$ is a geometric mean if $A \odot_\lambda B$ is measurable, $A \odot_\lambda B \subseteq \lambda A + (1-\lambda)B$, and $(sA) \odot_\lambda (tB) = s^\lambda t^{1-\lambda}(A \odot_\lambda B)$ for all $s,t > 0$.

nodes.name: Log-Brunn-Minkowski inequality for a measure
nodes.statement: A Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfies the log-Brunn-Minkowski inequality in $\mathcal{K}$ with geometric mean $\odot$ if $\mu(A \odot_\lambda B) \geq \mu(A)^\lambda \mu(B)^{1-\lambda}$ for all $A,B \in \mathcal{K}$, $\lambda \in [0,1]$.

nodes.name: Symmetric geometric mean $\odot^S$
nodes.statement: $A \odot_\lambda^S B = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : \langle x,u\rangle \leq h_A^\lambda(u) h_B^{1-\lambda}(u),\ \forall u \in S^{n-1}\}$, where $h_A$ is the support function of $A$.

nodes.name: Ideal geometric mean $\odot^I$
nodes.statement: $A \odot_\lambda^I B = \bigcup_{x \in A, y \in B} \prod_{i=1}^n [-|x_i|^\lambda |y_i|^{1-\lambda},\ |x_i|^\lambda |y_i|^{1-\lambda}]$.

nodes.name: $s$-concave measure
nodes.statement: A measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $s$-concave ($s>0$) if $\mu(\lambda A + (1-\lambda)B)^s \geq \lambda\mu(A)^s + (1-\lambda)\mu(B)^s$ for all non-empty compact $A,B$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$.

nodes.name: Log-concave measure
nodes.statement: A measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is log-concave if $\mu(\lambda A + (1-\lambda)B) \geq \mu(A)^\lambda \mu(B)^{1-\lambda}$ for all compact $A,B$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$.

nodes.name: Nice pair $(\mathcal{K},\mu)$
nodes.statement: A pair $(\mathcal{K},\mu)$ is nice if (a) $\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{K}_I$ and $\mu$ is unconditional product with decreasing density on $\mathbb{R}^n$, or (b) $\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{K}_I$ and $\mu$ is unconditional log-concave on $\mathbb{R}^n$, or (c) $\mathcal{K}=\mathcal{K}_S$ and $\mu$ is even log-concave on $\mathbb{R}^2$.

nodes.name: First mixed volume $V_1^\mu(A,B)$
nodes.statement: $V_1^\mu(A,B) = \frac{1}{n} \liminf_{t \to 0^+} \frac{\mu(A+tB) - \mu(A)}{t}$, the first mixed volume of $A,B$ with respect to $\mu$.

nodes.name: $\mu$-surface area $\mu^+(\partial A)$
nodes.statement: $\mu^+(\partial A) = \liminf_{t \to 0^+} \frac{\mu(A+tB_2^n) - \mu(A)}{t}$. Equivalently $\mu^+(\partial A) = n V_1^\mu(A, B_2^n)$.

nodes.name: Functional $M_\mu(A)$
nodes.statement: For a measure $\mu$ with density $e^{-\psi}$, $M_\mu(A) = \int_A \langle x, \nabla \psi(x)\rangle\, d\mu(x)$. For Gaussian, $M_{\gamma_n}(A) = \int_A |x|^2\, d\gamma_n(x)$.

nodes.name: Brunn-Minkowski for unconditional product measures with decreasing density (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be an unconditional product measure with decreasing density on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then $\mu$ satisfies the Brunn-Minkowski inequality in the class $\mathcal{K}_I$ of all ideals in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
assumptions: $\mu$ is an unconditional product measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$

nodes.name: Brunn-Minkowski for symmetric convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with even log-concave measure (Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with an even log-concave density. Then $\mu$ satisfies the Brunn-Minkowski inequality in the class $\mathcal{K}_S$ of all symmetric convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

nodes.name: Log-Brunn-Minkowski for unconditional log-concave measures on ideals (Theorem 3, cited)
nodes.statement: The log-Brunn-Minkowski inequality holds with geometric mean $\odot^I$ for any measure with unconditional log-concave density in the class $\mathcal{K}_I$ of ideals in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
assumptions: $\mu$ has an unconditional log-concave density on $\mathbb{R}^n$
nodes.origin_citation: Cordero-Erausquin, Fradelizi, Maurey 2004 (Proposition 8); also Saroglou (Proposition 4.2 in [S1])

nodes.name: Brunn-Minkowski for unconditional log-concave measures on ideals (Theorem 4)
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be an unconditional log-concave measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Then $\mu$ satisfies the Brunn-Minkowski inequality in the class $\mathcal{K}_I$ of all ideals in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
assumptions: $\mu$ is an unconditional log-concave measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$

nodes.name: Prékopa-Leindler inequality (cited)
nodes.statement: If $f,g,m \geq 0$ are measurable on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $\lambda \in [0,1]$, and $m(\lambda x + (1-\lambda)y) \geq f(x)^\lambda g(y)^{1-\lambda}$ for all $x,y$, then $\int m\,dx \geq (\int f\,dx)^\lambda (\int g\,dx)^{1-\lambda}$.

nodes.name: Borell characterization of $s$-concave measures (cited)
nodes.statement: A measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with non-degenerate support is log-concave iff its density has form $\varphi = e^{-V}$ with $V$ convex; $\mu$ is $s$-concave with $s \in (0,1/n)$ iff its density $\varphi$ satisfies $\varphi^{s/(1-sn)}$ concave; for $s=1/n$, $\varphi(\lambda x + (1-\lambda)y) \geq \max(\varphi(x),\varphi(y))$.

nodes.name: Ehrhard's inequality (cited)
nodes.statement: For non-empty compact $A,B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$: $\Phi^{-1}(\gamma_n(\lambda A + (1-\lambda)B)) \geq \lambda \Phi^{-1}(\gamma_n(A)) + (1-\lambda)\Phi^{-1}(\gamma_n(B))$, where $\Phi(t) = \gamma_1((-\infty,t])$.

nodes.name: Gaussian isoperimetric inequality (cited)
nodes.statement: For any measurable $A \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and any $t>0$, $\gamma_n(A_t)$ is minimized, among all sets with prescribed measure, by half-spaces $H_{a,\theta} = \{x : \langle x,\theta\rangle \leq a\}$.

nodes.name: S-inequality (cited)
nodes.statement: For $t>1$ and any symmetric convex body $A$, $\gamma_n(tA)$ is minimized, among subsets with prescribed measure, by strips $S_L = \{x : |x_1| \leq L\}$.

nodes.name: Unconditional Prékopa-Leindler with parameter (Proposition 1)
nodes.statement: Fix $\lambda,p \in (0,1)$. If $m,f,g$ are unconditional decreasing non-negative functions and $\mu$ an unconditional product measure with decreasing density on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $m(\lambda x + (1-\lambda)y) \geq f(x)^p g(y)^{1-p}$, then $\int m\,d\mu \geq [(\lambda/p)^p ((1-\lambda)/(1-p))^{1-p}]^n (\int f\,d\mu)^p (\int g\,d\mu)^{1-p}$.
assumptions: $\mu$ is an unconditional product measure with decreasing density

nodes.name: Log-BM with radially decreasing density implies BM (Proposition 2)
nodes.statement: If $\mu$ has a radially decreasing density $f$ (i.e. $f(tx) \geq f(x)$ for $t \in [0,1]$) and satisfies the log-Brunn-Minkowski inequality with geometric mean $\odot$ in class $\mathcal{K}$, then $\mu$ satisfies the Brunn-Minkowski inequality in $\mathcal{K}$.
assumptions: $\mu$ has a radially decreasing density $f$, i.e. $f(tx) \geq f(x)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $t \in [0,1]$
$\mu$ satisfies log-BM with geometric mean $\odot$ in $\mathcal{K}$
conclusions: $\mu$ satisfies the Brunn-Minkowski inequality in class $\mathcal{K}$

nodes.name: Reformulation with parameter $p$ (Lemma 1)
nodes.statement: Let $A,B$ be ideals in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mu$ an unconditional product measure with decreasing density. For any $\lambda \in [0,1]$ and $p \in (0,1)$: $\mu(\lambda A + (1-\lambda)B) \geq \left[(\lambda/p)^p ((1-\lambda)/(1-p))^{1-p}\right]^n \mu(A)^p \mu(B)^{1-p}$.
assumptions: $\mu$ is unconditional product with decreasing density

nodes.name: One-dimensional Brunn-Minkowski for unconditional measure (Lemma 2)
nodes.statement: Let $A,B$ be symmetric intervals and $\mu$ unconditional with decreasing density on $\mathbb{R}$. Then $\mu(\lambda A + (1-\lambda)B) \geq \lambda \mu(A) + (1-\lambda)\mu(B)$ for $\lambda \in [0,1]$.

nodes.name: Concavity of parallel volume (Corollary 1)
nodes.statement: Suppose $(\mathcal{K},\mu)$ is a nice pair and $A,B \in \mathcal{K}$ are convex. Then $t \mapsto \mu(A + tB)^{1/n}$ is concave on $[0,\infty)$.

nodes.name: Brunn-type theorem for $\mu$-sections (Corollary 2)
nodes.statement: Suppose $(\mathcal{K},\mu)$ is a nice pair, $A \in \mathcal{K}$ convex, and $\varphi$ the density of $\mu$. Then $t \mapsto \mu_{n-1}(A \cap \{x_1 = t\})$ is $\frac{1}{n-1}$-concave on its support.

nodes.name: Mixed Gaussian isoperimetric / reverse-S inequality (Corollary 3)
nodes.statement: For $A$ an ideal in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (or symmetric convex in $\mathbb{R}^2$) and $r>0$: $r\gamma_n^+(\partial A) + M_{\gamma_n}(A) \geq n\gamma_n(rB_2^n)^{1/n}\gamma_n(A)^{1-1/n}$, with equality for $A = rB_2^n$.
assumptions: $A$ is an ideal in $\mathbb{R}^n$, or a symmetric convex set in $\mathbb{R}^2$

nodes.name: Minkowski-first-type inequality for nice pairs (Corollary 4)
nodes.statement: Let $A,B \in \mathcal{K}$ with $(\mathcal{K},\mu)$ a nice pair. Then $V_1^\mu(A,B) + \frac{1}{n} M_\mu(A) \geq \mu(B)^{1/n} \mu(A)^{1-1/n}$. Specializing $B = rB_2^n$: $r\mu^+(\partial A) + M_\mu(A) \geq n\mu(rB_2^n)^{1/n} \mu(A)^{1-1/n}$.

nodes.name: Geometric means $\odot^S, \odot^I$ are valid (Remark 1)
nodes.statement: Both $\odot^S$ on $\mathcal{K}_S \times \mathcal{K}_S$ and $\odot^I$ on $\mathcal{K}_I \times \mathcal{K}_I$ are geometric means; verification uses $a^\lambda b^{1-\lambda} \leq \lambda a + (1-\lambda)b$.

nodes.name: Equality cases in Theorems 2 and 4 (Remark 2)
nodes.statement: Equality in Theorems 2 and 4 occurs only when $A$ is a dilation of $B$. If the density of $\mu$ is strictly decreasing then equality forces $A = B$.

nodes.name: Non-product unconditional density violates BM (Example 1)
nodes.statement: Take $C = \{|x|,|y| \leq 1\} \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ and density $\varphi(x) = \frac12 \mathbf{1}_{2C}(x) + \frac12 \mathbf{1}_C(x)$ (unconditional, not product). Then $\psi(a) = \sqrt{\mu(aC)} = \sqrt{2a^2 + 2}$ for $a \in [1,2]$ is strictly convex, so $\mu$ violates the BM inequality.

nodes.name: Unconditional product measure fails BM on non-unconditional symmetric set (Example 2)
nodes.statement: Take $\mu = \mu_0 \otimes \mu_0$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $\mu_0$ density $\varphi(x) = p + (1-p)\mathbf{1}_{[-1/\sqrt{2},1/\sqrt{2}]}(x)$. Rotating by $\pi/4$ and $R = [-1,1] \times [-\lambda,\lambda]$ for $0<\lambda<1/2$ yields $\psi(a) = \sqrt{\mu(aR)}$ strictly convex for $p \in (0,1)$, so unconditionality of sets cannot be dropped in Theorem 1.

nodes.name: BM inequality for symmetric sets and even log-concave measures
nodes.statement: Does Theorem 1's BM inequality hold for arbitrary symmetric sets $A,B$ when $\mu$ has even log-concave (not necessarily product) density? If not, does it hold under the additional assumption that $\mu$ is product? In particular, can the unconditionality assumption be removed in the Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality?

nodes.name: Gardner-Zvavitch conjecture (cited)
nodes.statement: Conjecture: $\gamma_n(\lambda A + (1-\lambda)B)^{1/n} \geq \lambda\gamma_n(A)^{1/n} + (1-\lambda)\gamma_n(B)^{1/n}$ holds for closed convex sets with $0 \in A \cap B$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$. Open in general; the present paper settles the 2D case for symmetric convex sets.

nodes.name: Classical Brunn-Minkowski inequality (eq. clasBM)
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{vol}_n(\lambda A + (1-\lambda)B)^{1/n} \geq \lambda \mathrm{vol}_n(A)^{1/n} + (1-\lambda) \mathrm{vol}_n(B)^{1/n}$.

nodes.name: Optimal $p$ choice (eq. p, optp)
nodes.statement: $p = \dfrac{\lambda \mu(A)^{1/n}}{\lambda \mu(A)^{1/n} + (1-\lambda)\mu(B)^{1/n}}$.

nodes.name: Differential identity for $M_\mu$ (eq. infs)
nodes.statement: $\partial_t \mu(tA)\big|_{t=1} = n\mu(A) - \int_A \langle x, \nabla \psi(x)\rangle\,d\mu(x) = n\mu(A) - M_\mu(A)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 from Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 1 with the optimal $p = \lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}/[\lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}+(1-\lambda)\mu(B)^{1/n}]$; this collapses the right-hand side to $(\lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}+(1-\lambda)\mu(B)^{1/n})^n$. Handle $\mu(B)=0$ separately using $0 \in B$ and decreasingness of the density.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\mu(A)\mu(B)>0$ and pick optimal $p$
nodes.statement: Assume $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and $\mu(A)\mu(B)>0$. Choose $p = \lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}/(\lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}+(1-\lambda)\mu(B)^{1/n}) \in (0,1)$.

nodes.name: Plug $p$ into Lemma 1
nodes.statement: With this $p$, $\frac{\lambda}{p}=\frac{\lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}+(1-\lambda)\mu(B)^{1/n}}{\mu(A)^{1/n}}$ and similarly for $\frac{1-\lambda}{1-p}$. Substituting in Lemma 1's bound gives $\mu(\lambda A+(1-\lambda)B) \geq (\lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}+(1-\lambda)\mu(B)^{1/n})^n$.

nodes.name: Degenerate case $\mu(B)=0$
nodes.statement: If $\mu(B)=0$, since $0 \in B$ we have $\lambda A \subseteq \lambda A+(1-\lambda)B$. Using decreasingness of the density: $\mu(\lambda A) = \lambda^n \int_A \varphi(\lambda y)\,dy \geq \lambda^n \mu(A)$, hence $\mu(\lambda A+(1-\lambda)B)^{1/n} \geq \lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1 from Proposition 1
nodes.statement: Take $m = \mathbf{1}_{\lambda A+(1-\lambda)B}$, $f = \mathbf{1}_A$, $g = \mathbf{1}_B$; these are unconditional decreasing and verify $m(\lambda x + (1-\lambda)y) \geq f(x)^p g(y)^{1-p}$. Apply Proposition 1.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1 by induction on $n$
nodes.statement: Induct on $n$. Base case $n=1$ uses normalization $\|f\|_\infty=\|g\|_\infty=1$, level-set inclusion $\lambda\{f>t\}+(1-\lambda)\{g>t\} \subseteq \{m>t\}$ and Lemma 2. Inductive step decomposes $\mu = \mu_1 \times \bar\mu$, applies the IH on $\bar\mu$, then Lemma 2 on $\mu_1$.

nodes.name: Base case $n=1$: normalization and level-set inclusion
nodes.statement: Normalize $f,g,m$ so $\|f\|_\infty=\|g\|_\infty=1$; the hypothesis is preserved if $c_m=c_f^p c_g^{1-p}$. Then for $t\in(0,1)$, $\lambda\{f>t\}+(1-\lambda)\{g>t\}\subseteq\{m>t\}$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2 (1D unconditional BM) and AM-GM
nodes.statement: Layer-cake: $\int m\,d\mu = \int_0^\infty \mu(\{m>t\})\,dt \geq \lambda \int f\,d\mu + (1-\lambda)\int g\,d\mu$ via Lemma 2. Then by $pa+(1-p)b \geq a^p b^{1-p}$ regrouping yields the claimed factor $(\lambda/p)^p((1-\lambda)/(1-p))^{1-p}$.

nodes.name: Inductive step: slice $\mu = \mu_1 \times \bar\mu$
nodes.statement: Define $m_{z_0}(x) = m(z_0,x)$ etc.; check $m_{\lambda x_0+(1-\lambda)y_0}(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)y) \geq f_{x_0}(x)^p g_{y_0}(y)^{1-p}$.

nodes.name: Apply IH on $\bar\mu$, then 1D case on $\mu_1$
nodes.statement: By the inductive hypothesis applied to $\bar\mu$, the integrated functions $M(z_0), F(x_0), G(y_0)$ (defined via $\bar\mu$-integration) are unconditional decreasing on $\mathbb{R}$ and satisfy $M(\lambda x_0+(1-\lambda)y_0) \geq F(x_0)^p G(y_0)^{1-p}$. Apply the $n=1$ case to $\mu_1$ to get the full claim.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2
nodes.statement: Use $A\odot_p B \subseteq pA+(1-p)B$ and rescale via $A' = (\lambda/p)A$, $B' = ((1-\lambda)/(1-p))B$. With $t = (\lambda/p)^p((1-\lambda)/(1-p))^{1-p} \in [0,1]$ and the radial decreasingness of $f$, deduce $\mu(tC) \geq t^n \mu(C)$. Combine with log-BM and the optimal $p$ choice.

nodes.name: Use geometric mean inclusion to bound $\mu(\lambda A + (1-\lambda)B)$
nodes.statement: Write $\lambda A+(1-\lambda)B = p\cdot(\lambda/p)A + (1-p)\cdot((1-\lambda)/(1-p))B$. Apply $((\lambda/p)A)\odot_p((1-\lambda)/(1-p)B)\subseteq p(\lambda/p)A + (1-p)((1-\lambda)/(1-p))B$ and homogeneity of $\odot_p$.

nodes.name: Use radial decreasingness: $\mu(tC) \geq t^n \mu(C)$
nodes.statement: Set $t = (\lambda/p)^p((1-\lambda)/(1-p))^{1-p} \in [0,1]$, $C = A\odot_p B$. By the change of variables and $f(tx)\geq f(x)$: $\mu(tC) = t^n\int_C f(tx)\,dx \geq t^n\int_C f(x)\,dx = t^n\mu(C)$.

nodes.name: Combine with log-BM and optimize $p$
nodes.statement: Apply log-BM: $\mu(A\odot_p B) \geq \mu(A)^p \mu(B)^{1-p}$. Choosing $p = \lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}/(\lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}+(1-\lambda)\mu(B)^{1/n})$ collapses the bound to $(\lambda\mu(A)^{1/n}+(1-\lambda)\mu(B)^{1/n})^n$. The case $\mu(B)=0$ follows directly from $\mu(\lambda A) \geq \lambda^n \mu(A)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3 via Prékopa-Leindler
nodes.statement: For $A,B \in \mathcal{K}_I$ define on $[0,\infty)^n$: $f = \mathbf{1}_{A \cap [0,\infty)^n}$, $g = \mathbf{1}_{B\cap[0,\infty)^n}$, $m = \mathbf{1}_{(A\odot_\lambda^I B)\cap[0,\infty)^n}$. Lift via exponentials: $F(x) = f(e^{x_1},\ldots)\varphi(e^{x_1},\ldots)e^{x_1+\cdots+x_n}$ etc. Use log-concavity and unconditional decreasingness of $\varphi$ to verify Prékopa-Leindler hypothesis, deduce the inequality on $[0,\infty)^n$, then extend by unconditionality.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 1 (parallel volume)
nodes.statement: By convexity of $A,B$, $\mu(A+(\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2)B)^{1/n} = \mu(\lambda(A+t_1B)+(1-\lambda)(A+t_2B))^{1/n} \geq \lambda\mu(A+t_1 B)^{1/n}+(1-\lambda)\mu(A+t_2B)^{1/n}$ by the BM inequality from Theorem 1, 2, or 4.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2 (Brunn-type)
nodes.statement: By convexity of $A$, $\lambda A_{\{x_1=t_1\}} + (1-\lambda)A_{\{x_1=t_2\}} \subseteq A_{\{x_1=\lambda t_1+(1-\lambda)t_2\}}$. Apply the BM inequality to the sections to get $1/(n-1)$-concavity.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4 (Minkowski first)
nodes.statement: Use Theorem 1 (or 2/4) with $\lambda=1-\varepsilon$ and $\tilde A=A/(1-\varepsilon)$, $\tilde B=B$ to get $\mu(A+\varepsilon B)^{1/n} \geq (1-\varepsilon)\mu(A/(1-\varepsilon))^{1/n}+\varepsilon\mu(B)^{1/n}$. Differentiate at $\varepsilon=0$ and use the identity $\partial_t\mu(tA)|_{t=1} = n\mu(A) - M_\mu(A)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2 (1D unconditional BM)
nodes.statement: Reducing to $A=[-a,a]$, $B=[-b,b]$, the claim is equivalent to $t \mapsto \int_0^t \varphi(x)\,dx$ being concave on $[0,\infty)$, which is equivalent to $\varphi$ being non-increasing on $[0,\infty)$.
